key_insight: LLM-based guardrails can be turned into a denial-of-service target when crafted inputs force them into long reasoning loops, consuming excessive tokens and latency.
engineering_relevance: This exposes an availability risk in autonomous-agent safety layers, showing guardrails must be cost-bounded and robust not just against jailbreaks but also against resource-exhaustion attacks.
method: Beam-search payload optimization uses an LLM proposer plus a strategy bank to maximize guardrail reasoning length.
A mechanism-aware structural-mutation attack exploits schema-following behavior with lower compute overhead.
The attacks are tested across multiple guardrail designs and real agent deployments to assess transferability and impact.
evidence_signal: According to the abstract, optimized payloads transfer from one surrogate model to eight major model backbones, causing 13–63× token amplification and up to 148× latency amplification in end-to-end deployments.
watch_item: Defense designs should avoid introducing unbounded reasoning loops or shared-resource bottlenecks, since a single poisoned document may degrade co-located agents and system-wide throughput.
paper_title: From Shield to Target: Denial-of-Service Attacks on LLM-Based Agent Guardrails
